AUTHOR: Marrable
TITLE: Generalised deep learning model for semi-automated length measurement of fish in stereo-BRUVS
SPECIES: Head and tail keypoint classes across 319 species (59 families, 153 genera)
DATA: OzFish stereo-BRUVS dataset with EventMeasure head/tail length annotations; 13,555 stereo pairs of cropped fish after filtering
D2: Out-of-sample test = deployments/locations prefixed A and E (4154 pairs); in-sample B and G split 70/30 train/val
D_EV: Sec. 2.2: 'the data were given prefix letters in their filenames to indicate they were taken from different deployments and at different locations'; A and E 'made up the out-of-sample data'
R_EV: Sec. 4.4: 'An effort to separate in-sample and out-of-sample data was made ... by training and testing to data collected at different dates and locations.' (all within OzFish)
C_EV: no statement found (no confidence threshold reported; only 'the one with the highest confidence score was chosen')
E_EV: Sec. 2.5: 'the remaining 3954 automated measurements were then compared to the manual measurements made by the fish ecologists' (Pearson r = 0.99)
ARCH: YOLOv5 small head/tail detector + EventMeasure stereo photogrammetry
METR: Precision, recall, F1 (head/tail); Pearson r of DL vs human length
NOTE: Split by deployment/location prefix within OzFish -> D_ALL Y, but per P2 not external (R1=N) despite authors calling it out-of-sample generalisability. E5: reference is ecologists' manual stereo-video measurements on the same stereo-BRUVS footage (EventMeasure), not an independent measurement — coded 같은 영상의 사람 판독; verifier should check against instruction text listing stereo length as independent. C_ALL NR: no threshold reported but false positives are discussed (Sec 4.2), so N rule not met. Small/far fish (<200 px) excluded — size filter, not visibility. TYPE coded 기타 (keypoint-based length measurement). In-sample 70/30 split unit not stated.
